key_insight: Nanoindentation can mechanically trigger amorphous-to-bcc devitrification in refractory metals, and the ease of crystal formation varies strongly across the series with V easiest and W hardest.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amorphous refractory coatings can be ranked for contact-load stability, helping engineers choose compositions that better resist unwanted crystallization under service.
method: Melt-quenched amorphous V, Nb, Mo, Ta, and W to 300 K
Validated interatomic potentials against ab initio liquid radial distribution functions
Ran large-scale molecular dynamics nanoindentation and tracked bcc fraction versus depth
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a CFA metric from sigmoidal bcc-fraction depth curves, a roughly fourfold spread across metals, and a velocity scaling of CFA ∝ v^-m with mean exponent 1.08.
watch_item: Results come from molecular dynamics with fitted potentials, so transferability to real coatings, defects, and experimental loading rates may be limited.
paper_title: Crystal forming ability of amorphous refractory metals under nanoindentation: a molecular dynamics study
